headline: Record profit and adjusted EPS as assets and buybacks grow
summary_short: LPL Financial posted net income of $379 million ($4.74 diluted EPS), up 39% year-over-year and 6% sequentially, as total client assets rose 34% y/y to $2.6 trillion and adjusted EPS climbed 29% y/y to a record $5.84.
summary_long: Revenue grew 35% y/y to $5.19 billion on broad growth across advisory, commission, and asset-based fees; advisory assets rose 46% y/y to $1.5 trillion and now make up 60.4% of client assets. Gross profit rose 24% y/y as Core G&A grew a slower 22%, lifting adjusted pre-tax margin to 39.3% from 37.6%. Organic net new assets were $23 billion (4% annualized). LPL lowered its 2026 Core G&A outlook to $2,140-2,165 million. The Commonwealth conversion remains on track for Q4 2026 with run-rate EBITDA guidance raised to $435 million. Cash rose 25% q/q to $1.28 billion; the board approved a $2.5 billion buyback increase and LPL repurchased $309 million of stock.

drivers.explanation: Management cites 'continued momentum' and 'strong performance' with record adjusted EPS, improved operating leverage, and progress on the Commonwealth onboarding and resumed capital deployment.

Growth was broad-based: advisory revenue +53% y/y on higher advisory assets, total commission +19% y/y, and total asset-based revenue +19% y/y, only partly offset by a 40% y/y decline in net interest income.
Adjusted pre-tax margin expanded to 39.3% from 37.6% as gross profit grew 24% y/y while Core G&A grew a slower 22%, producing positive operating leverage.
